0.long_answer: The tumor suppressor gene in question is the p53 gene, also known as TP53. This gene spans approximately 20 kilobases and is located on the short arm (p arm) of chromosome 17, specifically at 17p13.1. p53 plays a crucial role in regulating cell cycle progression and apoptosis, acting as a key safeguard against genomic instability. Its mutation is frequently observed in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) as well as many other types of cancers, leading to loss of its tumor suppressor function.
